info.name: Fuel Route Optimizer
info.description: Plan the cheapest fuel stops between two US locations (500-mile range, 10 mpg, starts with a full tank). Requests 1-7 are in demo order. Most use "geometry": "none" so the response stays readable on screen; the route line is shown in the map view (request 9).

request.description: Shows: 2 stops, total_fuel_cost, start.resolved_by = "place_table" (local lookup, no geocoding call), meta.external_api_calls = 1 routing call.

item.name: 2 - Chicago to Dallas again (cached, 0 external calls)

request.description: Identical request. meta.external_api_calls.total is now 0 - the route came from cache.
Coordinate input: start.resolved_by = "coordinates". Long trip, several stops.

item.name: 4 - Seattle to Miami with stop_penalty 0 (cheapest fuel, more stops)

request.description: Same trip optimised for fuel cost alone: a slightly smaller fuel bill but many more stops. Compare with request 3 and with summary.fuel_only_optimum.

item.name: 5 - Boston to Washington DC (under 500 miles, no stop needed)

request.description: fuel_stops is empty and total_fuel_cost is 0 - the vehicle starts with a full tank. gallons_used is still reported.

item.name: 8 - Free-text address (the only case that calls a geocoder)

request.description: Not a "City, ST" match, so it falls through to Nominatim once and is cached: start.resolved_by = "nominatim", meta.external_api_calls.geocoding = 1.
Browser page: route line, numbered stops, plan summary. Open this in Chrome rather than Postman.

item.name: 10 - New York to Los Angeles (full response with route geometry)

request.description: Cross-country, including the GeoJSON LineString for the route. Large response - kept out of the main demo for readability.
The same endpoint also accepts GET, which is handy for quick browser checks.
Confirms the app is up and how many stations are loaded (6,626).
